alignments.note: Transitional adverb rendered by the single word Furthermore.
Article in attributive position governing πατέρας across the interposed genitive τῆς σαρκὸς ἡμῶν; rule 57 gives it the English the, and the head noun stands bare.

Correlative μέν: the ASV writes no indeed and marks the correlation nowhere, so rule 70 leaves it empty. A reference comparison will report this as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.
The genitive pronoun ἡμῶν is free and takes the supplied possessive our, so under rule 20 this article is displaced and realizes nothing; the case preposition of stays with σαρκός.
Rule 20 keeps the case preposition of with the noun where the article is displaced by the possessive; discontinuous under rule 15 because our intervenes.
Genitive pronoun realized by the possessive our.
Head noun bare, its determiner having gone to s002 under rule 57.

Inflected verb takes its English subject and lexical verb; rule 9 heads on had rather than on we. The Greek expresses both elements of ἔχω + παιδευτάς but the ASV spells both out as had and to chasten, so rule 73 does not join them and rule 2 splits the pair.
The predicate noun correctors is rendered by an infinitival clause; the infinitival to and the supplied object us are rule 7 helpers on it, and rule 17 heads on the lexical verb chasten.
Coordinating conjunction.
Rendered by the support-verb phrase gave them reverence; rule 17 heads on the meaning-bearing complement reverence rather than on the subject, the auxiliary-like gave, or the pronoun object.
Ordinary negative aligned to not; no negative indefinite stands with it, so rules 41 and 59 are not in question.
Adverbial accusative much. The projection's underdetermined reading at SBLGNT.HEB.12.9.v004 is compatible with the English and rule 12 forbids a new textual decision here.
μᾶλλον rendered rather.

Future indicative taking its auxiliary shall and subject we; rule 17 heads the support phrase be in subjection on the meaning-bearing complement subjection. Discontinuous under rule 15, the intervening not much rather belonging to s012-s014.
Article with the case preposition riding along under rule 21, headed on the English the per rule 17.
Noun bare, its determiner taken by the article.

The ASV gives spirits no determiner, so this article has no the to anchor and is unrepresented under rules 21 and 23; the case preposition of stays with the noun. The marginal reading our spirits is not the text rendered.
Rule 21's determinerless case: of + noun stays one unit on the noun.
Expressed conjunction coordinating the two futures.
Future indicative sharing the earlier shall we; only the lexical verb is written again.

review_notes: s008/s009: the ἔχω + παιδευτάς pair is a light-verb construction, but rule 73 applies only where the ASV collapses the pair into a single English verb. Here it writes both had and to chasten, so rule 2 splits them.
s015 is deliberately discontinuous: shall we ... be in subjection wraps the negation and the comparative, which belong to s012-s014 under rule 27's warning against absorbing intervening words.
μέν (s003) is left unrepresented on the English-side test of rule 70; the answering clause carries no indeed and no other English word answers to it.
